To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

collagenase MMPs are expressed in normal breast epithelial and lobular carcinoma in situ (LCIS) tissue of LCIS patients, and that the expression of these markers does not differ between normal and LCIS tissue, suggesting that collagenase MMP expression in LCIS does not increase as the tissue transitions from benign to preinvasive.

MMP2 and MMP9 were not differentially expressed in lobular carcinoma in situ and normal breast tissue, and that MMP2 and 14 expression correlated with each other in lobular carcinoma and normal breast tissue.

MMP expression was not increased in LCIS compared to normal breast tissue, suggesting that collagen IV is unlikely to be degraded in the LCIS microenvironment, and therefore, that collagen IV may be a potential biomarker to distinguish normal from LCIS breast tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of MMPs and collagen IV in breast epithelium and the relationship between expression and the proliferative state of the tissue.
the role of collagenase MMPs in the pathogenesis of LCIS.
the role of matrix metalloproteinase (MMPs), which are enzymes that degrade extracellular matrix (ECM), in the progression of LCIS to breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
collagenase MMPs are not upregulated in LCIS compared to normal tissue, suggesting that the collagenase MMPs do not increase in LCIS compared the normal tissue.
MMP expression is not higher in LCIs compared with normal breast tissue, but this does not preclude a role for MMPs in the development or progression of breast cancer.
MMP2, 9 and 14 are expressed in normal breast tissue, but expression is not significantly different between normal breast tissue and LCIS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MMPs are expressed in LCIS and normal breast epithelium and that expression does not differ between these two types of breast epithelium.

MMP2, MMP9 and MMP14 are expressed in normal breast epithelium and in LCIS lesions of patients with LCIS, and that expression of these markers does not increase as a function of proliferative phenotype.
collagen IV expression is reduced in LCIS and normal breast tissue compared with normal breast tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MMP2 and MMP9 expression in LCIS is not increased relative to normal breast epithelium.
MMP expression does not appear to differ between LCIS and adjacent non-diseased breast tissue, which may be due to the fact that the LCIS cells are not actively degrading collagen.
